lines.text: There are only twenty-three people in this room.
And it's more likely that two of them share a birthday than not.
Twenty-three. Not one hundred eighty-three. Twenty-three.
It sounds impossible, I know. A year has three hundred sixty-five days.
Your gut is asking the wrong question.
It asks: will someone share my birthday? That's only about six percent.
The real question is about pairs. Any two people, anyone with anyone.
Two people make one pair. Ten make forty-five. Twenty-three make two hundred fifty-three.
Two hundred fifty-three chances for two dates to collide.
That's why the odds shoot up. With twenty-three, it's past fifty percent. With seventy, ninety-nine point nine.
We filled a hundred thousand rooms of twenty-three. In more than half, two people shared a birthday.
A football match has twenty-two players and a referee. Twenty-three.
So in about half of all matches, two people on the pitch share a birthday.
Now the real test. Write your birthday in the comments.
With just twenty-three of you, two will probably match. How many pairs will we find?
